title: Launch HN: Versine (YC F26) – MCP to send and receive money
text: Hey HN, we’re Harshith, Param, and Vishnu and we're building Versine ( https://versine.com ). Versine lets you send and request money just by talking or texting with your AI (think Venmo with an MCP). We’re software engineers who have worked on distributed systems at Stripe, Databricks, and Amazon. Versine is an MCP that sits in front of a wallet with a balance. With it, your agent can do things like: - Send money to someone with your approval (via passkey in our app) - Send and request money to/from up to 100 people at once - Send money to people without a Versine account (they cash out to their bank in 2 mins) - Pay people without your explicit approval to trusted contacts (you can set this) Here’s a demo: https://youtube.com/shorts/Q9X7zioEqi0 We started working on this because assistants are frustratingly hands-off when it comes to finance and money movement. You can have your assistant go through a receipt and map out all the amounts owed taking care of splitting the subtotal, taxes, tips, but at the end of it the assistant hands back work to you when you have to go out and make the Venmo transfer. Our current solution is oriented towards power users: those who want to automate everything through their agent use us to split dinners, group trips, or settle poker ledgers. We see ourselves unlocking more value for the general consumer as 1. More people turn into power users of agents, and 2. We expand to a more complete banking solution: deposits, transfers, wires, everything you can (and more) do with your bank offered as an MCP. Behind the scenes, each user has a self-custodial stablecoin wallet storing USDC on Base. With self-custodial wallets, users own their keys, meaning money can’t be sent without their approval. Interestingly, we were almost forced into this solution because we had around 4 weeks to build this product (after a pivot), and traditional fiat with a partner bank would have caused far too many regulatory and compliance slowdowns. Because of that, the only fast option that remained was using stablecoin wallets. It also ensures we aren't a Money Services Business (MSB) since we don’t hold control or access to the user’s funds. Each call to the wallet creates what we call one-time or recurring standing permissions. For a one-time payment, your agent makes an MCP call, and you receive a notification in our mobile app. Once you swipe up in the app and approve with a passkey (or your device’s biometric method), we create a one-time permission that instructs your wallet to send $X to your recipient’s address. Trusted contacts let your agent send money to people that you’ve previously authorized without explicit passkey approval. Generally, these are people that you’d trust to send your money back even if your agent made a mistake. We’re also able to support sending money to someone off Versine using claim forwarding, where the user authorizes us to forward a specific amount to a future address (which we create once we verify a recipient's OTP). Param worked on scaling vector search at Databricks and harness evals at Glean. Harshith worked on core Stripe Connect fee-processing infrastructure and built an AWS Fargate autoscaler at Amazon. Vishnu worked on intent-based agent testing infrastructure at Amazon. None of us were experienced in stablecoin or crypto infra before working on Versine but our distributed systems experience has helped us a lot. We'd love for you guys to try it! It's available on iOS and Android and as an MCP on ChatGPT and Claude. We also support a public MCP and REST API for other agents. Please let us know how you find it and if it works as you'd hoped! https://versine.com

title: I got $487 MRR in 3 days with zero ads. the exact distribution process I used
text: A few weeks ago I launched a product for accountant, to get easier the info of clients. No audience, no ad budget. no knowledge about accountant or similar arguments. Here’s what actually i did to get this numbers (487 are low, but guys in 3 days is crazy i think): 1. Where I posted sub-reddit, x, and linkedin. in first case, i try to give people real advice, and you know, try to get interest them in the thing. i don't want start the conversation: "i have problem x" and i reply "use my product" it's not like this that the things works. So i created first of all interest, and in reality everything comes naturally. for X and Linkedin (Linkedin my fav) bascially i tryed to build something on me, in this case the topic building in public, helped me a lot, beacause i got: Engagment People People money That's all. Just keep consistent, and everything will arrive! 2. The post format that worked: like i said before, the topic building in public worked very good for me: "day 7 of building ... Today i improve the product and now it is faster, i need beta tester to test it out" cleary, it was longer and more specific, this is only a "type-post" that i used to do. 3. What I did with comments: for the first, i was like: ok, now with this comments? My Reddit posts have always performed quite well I’ve never run into any issues often ending up with 30 or more comments, leaving me wondering how to handle them. Because of this, I would try to spark a conversation (just as I mentioned earlier) by engaging potential customers and subtly bringing up the product. Honestly, it was very difficult to hold back from just saying, "Here’s the product go get it!" but I wasn't sure how the customer might react. More importantly, I wanted to avoid coming across as the typical founder who’s just hunting for customers. 4. What flopped: X. Actually, i expected much from X, but the clients are very low, and i think that i may close it now. a huge flop my guys. Honestly the hardest part wasn’t any single tactic. It was knowing what to do each day and tracking what worked. I managed it all with messy spreadsheets and notes. So I’m turning that process into a simple tool for solo founders: tells you where to post, what format to use, and what’s actually bringing signups. If you’re struggling with distribution, drop your product below. I’ll suggest 2–3 places to start for free, and I’ll pick a few people to try the tool early.

title: Ask HN: Am I the only one whose AI hype is cooling down a lot?
text: I am in the industry for 15+ years, studied CS, and actually, never really "liked" programming. It was a means to an end. I have written about programming (and published books), so don't get me wrong: I like the craft and I miss the sense of accomplishment after hours and days of struggling and fixing a problem with 2 lines of code. What I see in my personal spending and habits: I get free tokens from my company, and I spent between 3k-5k a month at the start of the year. Models got cheaper, but also: The usefullness ran its course a little bit for me. I still don't write code by hand, but when doing research, finding solutions, even some decisions (using Opus 5.5 and Astra 6.2 for example) are more and more questionable. I handed large research tasks to models, but even small questions like: "What do you think about these PR comments pointing out issues" (I need to be vague, working for a larger company), it didn't find even basic facts I found via Google and reading the docs for 2mins. I usually did higher level thinking, researched with the model, and then went to the implementation phase. But lately, I am not happy with both the research results (I continuesly have to narrow it down, go back, refine... I spend a day or 2 days refining, which in the end, I can do by myself now and actually feel a sense of accomplishment). Even the implementation isn't all that great. Maybe my bar for acceptable work is higher now, since these tools are not "magic" anymore. I think I gave them more leeway in the beginning because they wowed me. But now... not so much anymore. I even dread opening up Claude Code or Codex and I'd rather read and write code myself, and just give them smaller tasks, or once I nailed it down, I let a large chunk of code write by a model (because it "types" faster...). Am I alone? I read a lot of think pieces, I have agents working on my private dedicated server to maintain my machine and set up my self-hosting services. But more and more, I'd rather.... do it myself again, be more precise, and use it as a workhorse instead of a thinking researcher.

title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
text: RBI/2026-27/304 DOR.STR.REC.256/21-04-177/2026-27 November 23, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Please refer to Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025 . 2. On a review, and in exercise of the powers conferred by the section 21 and 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in the public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified. 3. The Amendment Directions shall come into effect from April 01, 2027. 4. The Amendment Directions modify the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025 as under: (1) Paragraph 27 shall be substituted by the following, namely: “27. The issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes under these Directions shall only be in a dematerialised form. The minimum ticket size shall be ₹1 crore at the time of issuance as well as at any subsequent transfers. The originator shall ensure that the agreement with the SPE requires the latter to put in place necessary arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository, stock exchange etc., as may be applicable, to ensure compliance with the minimum ticket-size requirement. Provided that securitisation notes with amortisation structures shall be permitted to be traded at amortised value, if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. Explanation: Ticket size, for the purpose of these directions, refers to the size of investment by a single investor.” (2) Paragraph 28 shall be substituted by the following, namely: “28. With respect to offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008, as amended from time to time, shall be complied with.” (3) Paragraph 28A shall be inserted as below: “28A. Transactions in securitisation notes issued prior to April 01, 2027, shall also be undertaken in compliance with the requirements mentioned in Paragraph 27 & 28 above.” (Vaibhav Chaturvedi) Chief General Manager
